newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mills lead Egyptian shares down.
newsitem.headline: Mills lead Egyptian shares down.

text.p: Milling shares led prices down on the Egyptian stock exchange on Monday but brokers described this as merely a temporary correction.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index fell 0.42 points to close at 235.75 points in heavy volume of 61.88 million pounds ($18.2 million).

But much of the volume came through some big transactions in rarely traded Cairo Light Industries. Shares worth more than 44 million pounds changed hands, apparently as part of a deal between institutional investors, brokers said.
In the open sector, mills again dominated trade but the upward trend of the past few weeks finally came to an end.
"In fact the whole market was down, except cements," said broker Mohamed Abdallah of EFG Hermes.
"Firstly, there's not enough cash in the market because of settlement problems. Then, mills have been going well for two to three weeks and it was time for a correction," he added.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills slipped 0.90 to 48.60 pounds, Central and West Delta Flour Mills lost 1.50 to close at 58.50, and East Delta Flour Mills shed 1.00 to end the day at 39.00.
Heliopolis Housing and Development was one of the big losers, on rumours that the state had changed its mind about letting the company go majority private, Abdallah said.
"People thought the government would keep only 20 percent. Now the rumour is that it will sell only five percent," he added. The government now holds 80 percent of the company.
The stock slipped 4.26 percent to close at 179.00 pounds.

Brokers said the partial privatisation of General Silos and Storage would go through the exchange on Tuesday under the "discovery price" mechanism -- the first time this has been used in the privatisation programme.
Investors put in bids for two days last week, with the minimum set at 37.00 pounds for each of the four million shares on offer -- 40 percent of the company.
The state will allocate shares starting with the highest bidders and stopping when they run out. Everyone will pay the price bid for the last batch of shares.
Brokers said the system had dampened the demand from individuals and even from institutions the issue would not be subscribed to the same level as some previous privatisations.
"It may be oversubscribed four times by institutions and the price won't be far above 37 pounds," said Abdallah.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 345.53 from 345.56 points on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 168.23 from 168.92 points.
